pull_request.title: feat: implement formatted_panic_payload lint (#108)
pull_request.body:
Closes #108

## Summary

Implements the `formatted_panic_payload` lint: `format!`, `panic!` with formatting arguments, and `.expect(&format!(..))` inflate compiled WASM size (core::fmt machinery, pulled in on every deploy) and spend CPU formatting a message on the failure path, where `panic_with_error!` + a `#[contracterror]` enum costs neither. The diagnostic points at that alternative.

## Call shapes covered (exactly three, as scoped by the issue)

1. Any `format!(...)` invocation â^@^T always flagged, since building a `String` via `core::fmt` is never free in `no_std`.
2. `panic!(...)` **only** when the macro call had at least one formatting argument. `panic!("plain literal")` (zero args) is not flagged â^@^T it never touches `core::fmt`.
3. `.expect(&format!(...))` â^@^T an `.expect()` call whose message argumentâ^@^Ys macro-expansion root is `format!`. A plain `.expect("literal")`, or `.expect(some_local_str)`, is not flagged. `.unwrap()` is argument-less so there is nothing to check on it directly, per the issueâ^@^Ys own note.

When `.expect(&format!(...))` fires, the nested `format!(...)` call is deliberately **not** independently reported a second time (both are visited as separate HIR nodes by the lint pass) â^@^T the pair collapses into one warning pinned at the more actionable `.expect(...)` call site. See `is_expect_format_message` in `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs`.

## Detection approach

Per the issueâ^@^Ys explicit warning against pattern-matching desugared HIR (e.g. `Arguments::new_v1`), this uses `clippy_utils::macros`: `root_macro_call_first_node` + `is_panic` + the `format_macro` diagnostic item identify each macro by its expansion site, not by the shape it expands to.

The one wrinkle: telling `panic!("literal")` (0 args) apart from `panic!("{}", x)` (1+ args) needs the *original* argument count, which the HIR no longer has once `panic!` is desugared. `clippy_utils::macros::FormatArgsStorage` exists for exactly this (see `useless_format`/`format.rs` in the pinned clippy_utils revision for how clippy itself uses it), but it has to be populated by an early-pass AST visitor before the late pass runs. This PR adds a small `FormatArgsCollector` early lint pass (mirroring clippyâ^@^Ys own `clippy_lints::utils::format_args_collector::FormatArgsCollector`, trimmed of the proc-macro-span edge case clippy handles, which isnâ^@^Yt relevant here) that records the AST `FormatArgs` nodes into a `FormatArgsStorage` shared with the late pass via `register_lints`.

## Test vs. contract code: the `#[cfg(test)]` signal

Per the issue, both `#[cfg(test)]` and `#[contractimpl]` were candidate signals for distinguishing contract code from test code. This PR uses **`#[cfg(test)]` only**, via `clippy_utils::is_in_test` (covers both a `#[test]` fn and any ancestor â^@^T function or module â^@^T marked `#[cfg(test)]`).

A `#[contractimpl]`-reachability analysis (proving an expression is only reachable from a contractâ^@^Ys public entrypoints) was considered and rejected for a first version: it would need whole-crate call-graph reasoning (indirect calls, trait dispatch, re-exports) that is fragile and invasive relative to this crateâ^@^Ys other lints, which stay single-function or bounded-depth. This means the lint fires on qualifying `format!`/`panic!`/`.expect()` usage anywhere in non-test code compiled into the checked crate, not only code reachable from a `#[contractimpl]` entrypoint â^@^T acceptable in practice since `cargo-cost-lint` is run against Soroban contract crates specifically. Full rationale is in `docs/lints/formatted_panic_payload.md`.

## Files

**New:**
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/formatted_panic_payload.rs` / `.stderr` â^@^T standalone UI fixture (per `DEVELOPING_LINTS.md` Ã§3 convention, not touching `ui/main.rs`)
- `docs/lints/formatted_panic_payload.md`

**Modified:**
- `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs` â^@^T lint + `FormatArgsCollector` early pass + registration (`LINT_METADATA` as `LintCategory::Compute`, `register_lints`)
- `docs/lints/README.md` (CPU/Compute table row), `docs/SUMMARY.md` (Lints entry), `README.md` (Features bullet + `budget.toml` example), `CHANGELOG.md` (Unreleased/Added)

## UI fixture coverage

- Flagged: `format!(...)` (captured-identifier and positional-arg forms), `panic!("...{}..." , a, b)`, `.expect(&format!(...))`
- Not flagged: `panic!("plain literal")` (0 args), `.expect("plain literal")`, `.expect(local_str)`
- `#[allow(formatted_panic_payload)]` suppression
- The same flagged patterns placed inside a `#[cfg(test)]` fn **and** inside an enclosing `mod tests { .. }` â^@^T confirmed not to fire in either case

The generated `.stderr` was reviewed by hand: exactly 4 warnings, each span covers the full macro/method call (not an inner sub-expression), and the `.expect(&format!(..))` case produces one warning at the `.expect(...)` call, not two.

## How to test locally

```bash
cd soroban_cost_lints
cargo test --lib ui   # note: NOT `cargo test --test ui` â^@^T there is no such target;
                       # the UI harness is the #[test] fn `ui()` inside src/lib.rs
```

From the repo root:
```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p soroban_cost_lints --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p soroban_cost_lints
```

## Known pre-existing failures (not introduced by this PR, not fixed by it)

- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` fails to even parse (unclosed delimiter) against its `.stderr` â^@^T pre-existing on `main`, called out explicitly in the task as out of scope.
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/redundant_val_conversion.rs` references a `redundant_val_conversion` lint that isnâ^@^Yt currently registered in `lib.rs` at all (`unknown lint` warnings) â^@^T pre-existing drift, unrelated to this change.
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/soroban_storage_in_loop.rs`â^@^Ys `.stderr` has drifted against the (pre-existing) `storage_write_without_read` lintâ^@^Ys output â^@^T pre-existing drift, unrelated.
- `cargo-cost-lint/src/main.rs` currently fails to compile on `main` itself (undefined `BudgetConfig`/`HashMap`, an invalid format string in a test) â^@^T confirmed via `git diff main -- cargo-cost-lint/src/main.rs` showing zero difference. This means `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` cannot succeed at the workspace level right now, independent of this PR. `soroban_cost_lints` on its own is clean under both `cargo clippy -p soroban_cost_lints --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p soroban_cost_lints` (aside from the three pre-existing UI-fixture mismatches above).

feat: implement formatted_panic_payload lint (#108)

Detect format!(...), panic!(...) with formatting arguments, and
.expect(&format!(...)) in non-test code, all of which pull core::fmt
string-formatting machinery into a #![no_std] Soroban contract,
inflating WASM binary size on every deploy and spending CPU on the
failure path. The diagnostic points at panic_with_error! with a

Detection uses clippy_utils::macros (root_macro_call_first_node,
is_panic, the format_macro diagnostic item) to key off each macro's
expansion site rather than pattern-matching the desugared HIR shape.
Telling panic!("literal") (cheap, zero args) apart from a formatted
panic!("{}...", x) requires the original argument count, which the
HIR no longer exposes after desugaring to Arguments::new_v1(...); a
new early pass (FormatArgsCollector, mirroring clippy's own pass of
the same name) records the pre-expansion AST FormatArgs nodes into a
shared FormatArgsStorage that the late pass queries.

Skips #[cfg(test)] code (function-level or an enclosing mod tests)
via clippy_utils::is_in_test. A #[contractimpl]-reachability analysis
was considered and rejected as too invasive/fragile for a first
version; see docs/lints/formatted_panic_payload.md for the full
rationale.

Adds a standalone UI fixture (ui/formatted_panic_payload.rs/.stderr)
covering all three flagged shapes, their non-triggering counterparts,
the #[allow(..)] suppression, and both cfg(test) forms.

fix: repair pre-existing compile and lint-registration corruption on main

cargo-cost-lint/build.rs, cargo-cost-lint/src/main.rs, and
cargo-cost-lint/src/config.rs each had two versions of the same
function concatenated by earlier bad merges, leaving unclosed
delimiters that failed `cargo fmt`/`cargo build` outright. main.rs is
rebuilt from the last commit where it compiled and passed tests
(e6664e8), with the lint_info.rs/lint_explanations.rs includes it was
still missing.

soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs had a duplicated LintMetadata entry, a
duplicated Visitor struct field with an orphaned match arm, duplicate
imports, a check_fn signature mismatch, a rename
(try_get_adt_def -> ty_adt_def) that missed 7 call sites, and —
the one actually breaking CI — six lints double-registered in
register_lints(), which panics the dylint driver at runtime.

None of this is reachable from the formatted_panic_payload lint added
earlier in this branch; it was already broken on main independently.

Hi @HassanKorey 👋

This PR currently has **merge conflicts with `main`** and can't be merged as-is. Please resolve them so we can move forward with the review.

```bash
git remote add upstream https://github.com/Tollcraft/soroban-cost-linter.git   # if not already added
git fetch upstream
git checkout <your-branch>
git rebase upstream/main      # or: git merge upstream/main
# resolve the conflicted files, then:
git add .
git rebase --continue         # or: git commit  (if you merged)
git push --force-with-lease    # plain 'git push' if you merged instead of rebased
```

A couple of reminders while you're at it:
- Make sure the branch still builds and `cargo test` passes after the rebase.
- Commit messages must follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — CI enforces this.

Ping us here once it's updated and we'll re-review. Thanks for contributing! 🙏
